name: K.C. Das
why_it_matters: Krishna Chandra Das opened this confectionery in 1930 with his son Sarada Charan; the family had carried Nobin Chandra Das's spongy rosogolla recipe forward from 1868. K.C. Das is credited with India's first canned dessert (canned rosogolla), which let Bengali sweets travel beyond the city for the first time.
insider_tip: Eat the rosogolla in-shop, not from the can — the cold-storage rosogolla at the Esplanade counter has a lighter syrup. Ask for one fresh from the tray, not the chilled stack.

name: Balaram Mullick & Radharaman Mullick
why_it_matters: Founded by Ganesh Chandra Mullick in 1885 in Bhowanipore; the dual-name comes from his brother Balaram and Balaram's son Radharaman who carried the shop forward. Reputed to have introduced baked sandesh in Kolkata. The Poddopukur Road flagship spans 11,000 sq ft today.
insider_tip: Nolen gur (date palm jaggery) sandesh is seasonal — November to February only. The baked sandesh travels well as a gift; the soft korapak doesn't survive a flight.

name: Indian Coffee House
why_it_matters: The Coffee Board first opened a coffee joint here in 1942 inside Albert Hall (1876); renamed Coffee House in 1947 and run as a workers' cooperative since the late 1950s. Adda haunt of Satyajit Ray, Sunil Gangopadhyay, Aparna Sen and generations of Presidency and Calcutta University students.
insider_tip: Operates on Bankim Chatterjee Street, not College Street proper — entrance is through a narrow staircase next to the books. Skip lunch hour (12-2pm); afternoon between 3-5pm is when the real adda regulars arrive.
signature_address: 15, Bankim Chatterjee Street, College Square, Kolkata 700073
